claim: The proxy provider is registered inside the onWillActivateFileSystemProvider handler, so every vscode-remote access re-registers it — throwing/logging an error each time and leaking an undisposed RemoteFileSystemProxyClient instance.
raw: The proxy provider is (re)registered inside the `onWillActivateFileSystemProvider` handler. Because `fileService.activateProvider` fires that event *before* its `if (this.provider.has(scheme)) return` early-out, every access to a `vscode-remote://` URI constructs a new `RemoteFileSystemProxyClient`

claim: On partial download failure the catch pushes all original remote URIs even though some temp targets were already added to result, so already-copied resources appear twice on the clipboard.
raw: On partial failure the catch runs `result.push(...remoteResources)` even though some temp targets were already added to `result`. ... `remoteA` now appears twice on the clipboard, so paste yields a duplicate/inconsistent set.

claim: hasResources() can return true while readResources() returns [] because has* checks any native clipboard format but read* filters to file:// only, enabling a Paste command that does nothing.
raw: `has*` checks any native clipboard format; `read*` filters to `file://` only. On Linux, a non-file `text/uri-list` entry makes `hasResources()` true, enabling the Paste command, but `readResources()` returns `[]` and the paste does nothing.

claim: plistToFiles parses NSFilenamesPboardType with an XML-plist regex, but Finder writes a binary plist, so the regex matches nothing and Finder-copied files can never be pasted.
raw: The read path intends to support Finder→VS Code paste, but Finder writes `NSFilenamesPboardType` as a **binary** plist (bplist). The XML regex `/<string>([^<]+)<\/string>/` matches nothing → returns `[]` → nothing pasted.

claim: setToCopy eagerly downloads the entire remote tree to a local temp dir before the clipboard write returns, hanging the copy and filling disk even if the user never pastes; in web every copy triggers a full download.
raw: `setToCopy` awaits `resolveClipboardResources` → `fileService.copy(remoteFolder, temp, true)`, downloading the entire remote tree before the clipboard write returns. The copy hangs and fills local disk even if the user never pastes.

claim: resolveClipboardResources emits all local files before all remote files, losing the original selection order for mixed selections.
raw: `resolveClipboardResources` emits all local files before all remote files. Selecting `[remoteA.ts, localB.ts]` produces `[localB.ts, tempA.ts]`. Any consumer relying on order (or the first entry) targets the wrong file.

claim: fileNameWToFile constructs a Uint16Array over the buffer's byteOffset, which throws RangeError on an odd offset; the try/catch swallows it so a validly copied Windows file can't be pasted.
raw: `new Uint16Array(buffer.buffer, byteOffset, len)` throws `RangeError` when the IPC-deserialized `VSBuffer` has an odd `byteOffset` (offset must be a multiple of 2). The try/catch swallows it → returns `[]`, so a validly copied single-file `FileNameW` can't be pasted.

claim: Remote resources no longer contribute DataTransfers.TEXT, so dragging a vscode-remote file into an editor or text field inserts nothing — a behavior regression.
raw: Remote resources no longer contribute `DataTransfers.TEXT` (only `file://` do now). Dragging a `vscode-remote` file into an editor/text field inserts no text; previously it inserted the path. Intentional for the Finder `.webloc` case, but a behavior regression for remote drag-to-text.

claim: The server's exists and resolve handlers, their switch cases, and resolve's IFileStatWithMetadata plumbing are unreachable dead code — the only client calls just stat/readdir/readFile.
raw: The only consumer (`RemoteFileSystemProxyClient`) is a filesystem provider that calls just `stat`/`readdir`/`readFile`. The `exists` (line 74) and `resolve` (line 78) methods plus their switch cases (lines 42-43) — and resolve's `IFileStatWithMetadata` plumbing — are never invoked.

claim: Temp clipboard copies are deleted on window dispose while the OS clipboard still references those paths, so a delayed native paste after closing the source window fails.
raw: Temp clipboard copies are deleted on window dispose (and on the next remote copy). If the user copies remote files then closes that window before pasting into Finder, `dispose()` deletes the temp dir while the OS clipboard still references those paths → native paste fails.

claim: The proxy provider is registered inside the onWillActivateFileSystemProvider handler, so it re-registers on every vscode-remote activation, causing error-log spam and a leaked provider instance each time.
raw: The proxy provider is (re)registered inside the onWillActivateFileSystemProvider handler, so it re-registers on every vscode-remote activation, causing error-log spam and a leaked provider instance each time.

raw: On partial download failure, the catch pushes ALL original remote URIs even though some temp targets were already added to result, duplicating the already-downloaded resources on the clipboard.
